Patek Philippe Calatrava Chronograph Instantaneous Perpetual Calendar Ref. 5978P For the first time, Patek Philippe is combining its manually wound chronograph movement with an instantaneous perpetual calendar in the new 500-component CH 29-535 PS QI caliber. The instantaneous perpetual calendar—previously seen in the Grand Complication Ref. 5207 from 2008, the triple complication Ref. 5208 in 2011, and the quadruple complication Ref. 5308 in 2023—advances all of the calendar displays simultaneously at midnight in 30 milliseconds. The chronograph is based on the caliber CH 29-535 unveiled in 2009. Together in the new caliber, which is regulated by a Gyromax balance with a Breguet overcoil balance spring, the movement, visible through the sapphire crystal caseback, oscillates at a frequency of 28,800 vibrations per hour with a power reserve between 55 and 65 hours, while the chronograph is disconnected. Limited to just 120 pieces, it is housed in a hand-polished 42 mm platinum Calatrava case and comes with a sunburst navy blue dial with a black-gradient rim, white-gold faceted applied baton-style hour markers, and luminous dauphine-style hands. The central chronograph hand is varnished in red, while the instantaneous 30-minute counter comes white-gold hand. Patek Philippe Calatrava Chronograph Instantaneous Perpetual Calendar Ref. 5978P Combining Patek Philippe’s instantly recognizable world time function with a minute repeater, these two exquisite references depict a map of Milan in cloisonné grand feu enamel—each limited to just five pieces. The Ref. 5531G-012 shows a view of the city’s downtown neighborhood by day (pictured left), while the Ref. 5531G-013 (pictured right) renders the same view by night. Both white gold 40.2 mm versions use 45 cm of gold wire and various hues of enamel to create the scene. Encircling these rare handcraft executions is the city disk with names displayed, naturally, in Italian with “Milano” standing out in red, while the case band and minute repeater slide are decorated by hand in Clous de Paris and hobnail guilloché. Local time is read on the pierced hour hand in white gold, inspired by the Southern Cross constellation. The Ref. 5531G-012 comes on a hand-stitched calfskin leather in light brown, while the Ref. 5531G-013 comes in dark blue calfskin leather, both with fold-over clasps in white gold. The references come with the R 27 HU self-winding movement comprising 452 parts. What makes these two new models particularly enticing is the fact that Patek Philippe has not debuted a world time minute repeater since the Ref. 5531R, which debuted in 2017 at the brand’s Grand Exhibition in New York. Plus, they are both delivered with interchangeable back covers—each with the inscription “Patek Philippe Milan 2026″—one in sapphire crystal and the other in white gold with hand engraving. And, secondary prices of the 2017 model are listed for over $1 million. Patek Philippe Rare Handcrafts World Time Minute Repeater Ref. 5531G Patek Philippe Aquanaut Ref. 5167A In keeping with the sportier vibe of many of the releases at this Patek Philippe Grand Exhibition, an Aquanaut was in order. This version, limited to 250, offers the coveted model in 40.8 mm in steel with a sunburst blue dial with a black-gradient rim, applied Arabic numerals in white gold with luminescent coating, and a pop of red on the seconds hand. The midnight blue strap matches the color scheme and comes with a fold-over clasp with four independent safety catches should you want to put its durability to the test…or ensure it doesn’t end up in someone else’s hands. The Ref. 5167 was first released in 2007 for the 10-year anniversary of the Aquanaut and in 2019, the model was upgraded with the caliber 26-330 S C, also housed in this new version. The refined movement added a hacking seconds and improvements to the winding and central-seconds mechanisms. Almost 20 years since its debut, this model remains an enduring and coveted staple of the Patek Philippe lineup. Patek Philippe Aquanaut Ref. 5167A Patek Philippe Perpetual Calendar Ref. 7147G Many of the new releases in Milan take cues from the hues of the Italian flag and this perpetual calendar in green is a particularly striking offering. The lacquered dial’s applied Arabic numerals in white offer crisp legibility against the rich background. Limited to 100, it is inspired by the Calatrava Ref. 6007 from 2020 and comes in a desirable 38 mm size in white gold. The green alligator leather strap keeps the overall feel of the watch as elevated as its complication. The stap is finished with topstitching that also mimic the Italian flag. Inside is the caliber 240 Q ultra-thin self-winding movement with a 22-karat gold micro-rotor, which keeps the interior construction thin at just 3.88 mm thick. Breitling Navitimer B09 Chronograph Tribute to Miles Davis This new retro design Breitling is inspired by the 1960s Breitling Navitimer ref. 806 Mk5, worn by Miles Davis. The manual caliber B09 is a nod to an era when automatic chronograph movements didn’t exist. The 41 mm case is steel, with a rally inspired “Air Racer” bracelet with round vents, or a gradient brown calf leather strap. It’s limited to 500 pieces, and a three-piece boxed set includes versions in stainless steel, 18-karat yellow gold, and platinum. On the bracelet alone, the model is priced at $9,600, the strap, $8,900. The entire boxed set will run you $96,400. Breitling Navitimer B09 Chronograph Tribute to Miles Davis Bulgari Octo Finissimo Dual Timer x Vianney Halter The new BVLGARI watch is a merger that preserves the signature elements of each: the rigorous geometry of the Octo Finissimo case with a movement made for the model, and the industrial details, multiple displays, and three-dimensional architectural complexity (the case consists of 50 components) of independent watchmaker Vianney Halter. It’s limited to 30 pieces in titanium, priced at $80,000, and 15 in pink gold, at $123,000. Bulgari Octo Finissimo Dual Timer x Vianney Halter Daniel Roth Extra Plat Rose Gold Gilt Daniel Roth‘s newest watch is here. The “gilt” in the timepiece’s name refers to the dial finish, created largely by hand following a multi-step technique that involves guilloché engraving and silicon pad transferral, along with electroplating and other treatments. The result is a unique 3-D effect that goes beyond simple pad printing or engraving. The case is 18-karat rose gold, and it comes on a black leather strap. Powered by the manual wound caliber DR002, the watch is priced at a cool $76,500. Daniel Roth Extra Plat Rose Gold Gilt Bremont Terra Nova Jumping Hour Bremont extends its Terra Nova Jumping Hour with five new pieces, headlined by an all-new 35mm case, the collection’s first dress-watch scale. A rich burgundy joins the established pink as Bremont’s second British colourway, offered across both the new 35mm and the original 40.5mm. It is a shrewd move by CEO David Cerrato, as the jumping hour and guichet trend remains strong, and both male and female collectors still eschew large sizes in favour of compact chic. Each version keeps the jumping hour’s bold montre à guichet display and BC634 calibre, switching the hour disc in under a tenth of a second. In steel and pink, this dressy number rounds out the family with a shimmer that’ll catch the eye of many collectors. Bremont Terra Nova Jumping Hour Zenith Chronomaster Solo Sport The new ZENITH Solo Sport is the first Chronomaster that is a three-hand rather than a chronograph version of the iconic El Primero movement, emphasizing the caliber’s defining feature: 5 Hz or 36,000 vph.
